issue.title: [Week 8 matchup study] T.J. Hockenson at Detroit — TE opportunity, matchup and competing explanations
issue.body:
## Question and working view

**Pregame snapshot: October 28, 2026. Minnesota at Detroit, Week 8.** We want to test whether T.J. Hockenson is a particularly strong one-week TE start or streaming option, with a plausible ceiling outcome. This is an exploratory research note, not a guarantee, formal model output, or a claim that he is available in any particular league.

Our working case combines Hockenson's target-earning role with Detroit's unusually high production allowed to tight ends. The strongest competing explanations are a short, opponent-heavy sample, touchdown volatility, changing defensive health, and Minnesota's limited passing volume and competition for targets.

## What we observed

**Minnesota TE distribution:** through Week 7, [LeagueLogs](https://leaguelogs.com/guides/nfl-target-share/teams/minnesota-vikings) reports 153 team targets and 46 TE targets: Hockenson 32 (69.6% of TE targets; 20.9% of all team targets), Gavin Bartholomew 8, Josh Oliver 5 and Ben Yurosek 1. These are full-season team-denominator shares, including games players missed or exited. Hockenson left early in Week 5; Bartholomew received six targets that game. In Week 7 Hockenson returned to 5 targets, 4 catches, 35 yards and a TD. [Week-by-week TE log](https://www.fftoday.com/stats/fantasystats.php?LeagueID=5&PosID=40&Season=2026&Side=Scored&TeamID=9022&o=2&order_by=GameWeek&sort_order=DESC); [Week 7 report](https://www.nbcsports.com/fantasy/football/player-news/2026-10-25/t-j-hockenson-scores-td-in-week-7-win).

[Fantasy Footballers' Week 8 route report](https://www.thefantasyfootballers.com/analysis/targets-per-route-run-report-week-8-fantasy-football-4/) lists Hockenson at 28.3% targets per route over 113 routes. Fantasy Points Data's screenshot shared in our discussion reports 0.28, tied with Trey McBride; the screenshot is the source for that tie, not an independently audited dataset. Thirteen of Hockenson's 32 targets came in one game, against Miami, affecting the season rate. [Game log](https://www.fftoday.com/stats/fantasystats.php?LeagueID=5&PosID=40&Season=2026&Side=Scored&TeamID=9022&o=2&order_by=GameWeek&sort_order=DESC).

A [player report](https://fantasydata.com/nfl/t-j-hockenson-fantasy/20805) identifies only two games both Kyler Murray and Hockenson started and finished: 17 catches on 18 targets, 154 yards and one TD. This is an overlapping, selected two-game sample, not an independent estimate of future production.

**Detroit matchup:** through six games, Detroit has allowed 29.4 PPR points per game to the TE position, including 56 catches, 602 yards and 10 receiving touchdowns. That's the aggregate across opposing TEs, not a projection for Hockenson. Sources may differ by scoring rules: [FF Today](https://www.fftoday.com/stats/fantasystats.php?LeagueID=5&PosID=40&Season=2026&Side=Allowed&TeamID=9020&o=2&order_by=TeamAbb&sort_order=ASC) reports 176.2 total PPR points (29.37/game), while [Pro Football Reference](https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2026/fantasy-points-against-TE.htm) reports 179.2 (29.9/game); the three-point difference is not reconciled.

| Week | Featured TE | PPR points |
|---|---|---:|
| 1 | Juwan Johnson | 14.4 |
| 2 | Dalton Kincaid | 22.5 |
| 3 | Kenyon Sadiq | 23.5 |
| 4 | Darren Waller | 6.6, on 6 targets |
| 5 | Trey McBride | 21.6 |
| 6 | Bye | — |
| 7 | Tucker Kraft | 14.8 |

These individual lines are consistent with [FF Today's player results](https://www.fftoday.com/stats/fantasystats.php?LeagueID=5&PosID=40&Season=2026&Side=Allowed&TeamID=9020&o=2&order_by=TeamAbb&sort_order=ASC). The positional total also includes Noah Fant's 13.3 in Week 1, Jeremy Ruckert's 14.9 in Week 3 and Arizona's Teagan Quitoriano and Elijah Higgins combining for 24.2 in Week 5. This is broader than the opposing featured TE alone.

## Questions that could strengthen or weaken the case

1. **Role and availability:** What were Hockenson's routes, route participation, targets, red-zone opportunities and first-read involvement when he, Murray, Jefferson and Addison were all available? What are the actual game samples and player availability? Separate measured routes from targets and note provider differences.
2. **Context behind Detroit:** Which TE matchups generated targets, yards and TDs, and how much came from game script, quality opponents, play volume, backups or unusual scoring? Compare opponent baseline and expected target/TD rates where reliable data exists. Avoid treating raw positional points as a pure coverage grade.
3. **Defensive personnel:** Which Lions defenders were unavailable in those games, who is expected back or limited for Week 8, and what evidence connects their roles to TE coverage? Verify Friday injury reports and Sunday inactives; do not assume a specific defender covered a TE without a witness.
4. **Game environment and competing options:** What passing volume, projected game script, protection and QB performance support the opportunity? Does Jefferson/Addison returning or Minnesota leaning on the run reduce Hockenson's target path? Compare credible TE alternatives and scoring formats if making a real lineup decision.
5. **Rate sensitivity:** How does his TPRR and target share look by game and with the 13-target Miami outing shown separately? Retain the full sample and identify any removed observations and denominators. Are the high-rate splits supported by enough routes?
6. **Mechanism:** Does the available evidence show a repeatable matchup advantage—alignment, route type, coverage and target depth—or only a descriptive fantasy-points correlation? Note unavailable charting rather than inventing it.

**Strengthening evidence:** sustained Hockenson route participation and target share with the other weapons present; matchup-specific TE opportunity beyond isolated TDs; current Detroit personnel or schematic evidence supporting a vulnerability; sufficient Minnesota pass volume.

**Weakening evidence:** high season target rate dominated by one unusual game, low route participation or target share with all weapons present, Detroit's relevant defenders returning, opponent-adjusted results much less extreme, or an expected low-volume Minnesota passing environment. Multiple TEs earning points does not establish that Minnesota will distribute opportunities similarly.

## One postgame update

After the Week 8 game, post one update here. Read this initial note and existing comments first; use final box scores plus available snap/route and target data. Record Hockenson and the entire Minnesota TE room's targets, catches, yards, TDs and PPR points; route participation and target share when sourced; team passing volume, game script, relevant availability and any visible matchup mechanism. Evaluate each original question as supported, challenged, mixed or unresolved, separating pregame process from one-game fantasy outcome. Identify missing or conflicting evidence. Preserve this pregame snapshot; do not retroactively alter the thesis. No recurring multi-week monitoring is requested.

Related background: [Week 7 Vikings research #49](https://github.com/Prometheus-Frameworks/TIBER-Research/issues/49).
